card.name: Inside all-caps titles and brand names
card.fires_on: Words inside ALL-CAPS text, such as titles, warning lines or brand names, usually partway through a phrase or name. Often it is a short word or word start where the capitalised phrase is still unfinished.

modes.label: All-caps titles
modes.description: Words within a capitalised book title or heading that is still unfinished.
modes.example: In 1973 it was included in Schumacher’s book SMALL IS BEAUTIFUL: ECONOMICS<< AS>> IF PEOPLE MATTERED.

modes.label: All-caps label warnings
modes.description: Words inside capitalised storage or overdose instructions on a drug label.
modes.example: THIS MEDICATION SHOULD BE KEPT IN A<< CHILD>>-RESISTANT CONTAINER AND OUT

modes.label: Repeated brand name start
modes.description: The first piece of a brand name such as SYNJARDY when it is repeated after 'or' or 'and'.
modes.example: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS SYNJARDY and<< SYN>>JARDY XR are contraind

card.writes: It seems to favour closing punctuation and quote marks, and to discourage common words like 'the'.
card.plain: It fires inside capitalised titles and warnings, or at the start of a repeated brand name, where the phrase is not yet finished.
